neighbours.label: the possessive pronoun after 'hold' in body idioms (hold your breath, hold my hand, holding her tongue); possessives after other verbs (lose, wash, find) stay low
fire: They say the bridge will reopen soon, but I wouldn't hold my breath.
The children were told to hold their tongues during the ceremony.
Nobody believes the promise, so don't hold your breath waiting for it.
She had to hold her nose as she walked past the old fish market.
The diver held his breath for almost three minutes.
During the storm he kept holding my arm so I wouldn't slip.
We are still holding our breath for the final results.
The nurse asked the boy to hold his arm still for the injection.
quiet: They say the bridge will reopen soon, but I lost my map of the city.

The diver found his mask lying on the bottom of the pool.
During the storm he kept checking my phone for weather alerts.
We are still painting our kitchen after three long weekends.
